title: Cross-SDK record-and-replay harness with time-freezing, redaction, and deterministic fixtures
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a reproducible record-and-replay test harness across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that covers streaming ergonomics, retries, and common example flows while keeping fixtures deterministic and safe to commit (no secrets).

Scope and motivation:
- We need stable CI tests that validate API surface and SDK behavior (retries, streaming chunk assembly, function-calling shapes) without flakiness from live model variations or network noise.
- Existing approaches (full output equality against raw recordings) are brittle when model variant or quantization changes. We will record representative scenarios but assert on stable contract properties, with a small set of golden exact-match fixtures for critical regressions (tokenization, structured output).

Design summary (high level):
1) Recording format: JSONL VCR-style records with metadata fields: request_hash, normalized_request, response_events, model_version, pinned_config. Files under tests/fixtures/vcr/<sdk>/<scenario>.jsonl. Each record normalized to remove timestamps, API keys, and ephemeral IDs.
2) Time-freezing: CI and local playback support a TIME_FREEZE flag. Streaming records include chunk sequence numbers; we normalize time deltas to fixed intervals during replay.
3) Determinism: We pin model_version and recommend temperature=0 for golden recordings. For non-deterministic cases (stochastic decoding), tests assert structural properties (presence/absence of fields, stable schema) rather than byte-exact content.
4) Redaction: A redaction pass runs over recordings to replace any found secrets (API keys, auth headers, user PII) and to canonicalize prompt placeholders. Redaction rules are documented and implemented as a single script tests/tools/redact_recording.py (used by all SDKs).
5) Streaming: Capture both HTTP chunked responses and websocket events. Represent streaming events as an ordered list of {type, delta, partial_text, token_ids_masked}. Replay preserves event ordering and delta sizes but normalizes timestamps. SDK tests exercise both event-driven handlers and convenience async iterators.
6) Per-SDK adapters: Each SDK implements a small adapter that translates its HTTP client or event emitter to/from our VCR record format. Python uses pytest-record-like harness; TS uses a custom recorder built on nock + stream-capture; Go uses go-vcr plus a small wrapper for chunked responses.
7) Contract tests vs golden fixtures: Contract tests verify request shapes (headers, body schema), route compatibility (status codes, error payload shapes), and high-level behavior (retry on 429/5xx with backoff). Golden fixtures are for a small set of canonical examples (streams assembling into a final JSON object, embeddings stable for seeded text) and are run on release branches only to catch regressions that require large rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Local dev flow: developers can record (RECORD=true) and produce a redacted fixture that can be committed
CI replay: pipeline job reproduces recordings deterministically and passes contract assertions across Python/TS/Go SDKs
Streaming correctness: tests validate SDK assembly of streaming chunks into final outputs for at least three real-world examples (chat, tool-calls, structured JSON streaming)
Retry behavior: contract tests assert SDKs retry on 429 with exponential backoff and stop after configured attempts
No secrets: redaction script removes any API keys, bearer tokens, and email addresses from committed fixtures
run_instructions: TypeScript (record): RECORD=true REDWOOD_API_KEY=live_key yarn test:record --testPathPattern=tests/vcr/chat-stream.spec.ts --out tests/fixtures/vcr/ts/chat-stream.jsonl
Go (record): RECORD=true REDWOOD_API_KEY=live_key go test ./sdk/go/... -run TestVCRRecord -recordFile=tests/fixtures/vcr/go/chat_stream.jsonl
ci_jobs: ci/sdk-vcr-golden-on-release (runs golden fixtures once per release branch)
updates: 2026-02-18 - Created: initial spec and prototype recorder for Python. Decided on JSONL as canonical on-disk format to simplify streaming event append and diffing.
2026-02-22 - Progress: TS team delivered nock-based adapter; we added stream-capture to preserve chunk boundaries. Initial fixtures for 'chat_stream' and 'function_call' recorded.
2026-02-26 - Design decision: avoid asserting full-text equality for most recordings. Use schema/contract assertions plus a small set of golden exact-match fixtures protected by release gating.
2026-02-28 - Review: Security reviewed redaction rules. Action item: add regex to scrub UUID-like IDs used in customer prompts (ENG-21700 as follow-up).

2026-03-01 - CI integration: added ci/sdk-python-vcr-replay job; discovered flaky replay when real network delay > normalized value. Mitigation: normalize timestamps and add small jitter tolerance in assertions.

2026-03-02 - Next steps: finalize redaction script, add lint job to CI to fail on non-redacted recordings, and write cross-SDK contract tests for retry/backoff behavior. Assign follow-up ENG-21745 to add sample fixtures for embeddings and reranking.
